A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we develop a generic approach to unify the existing VAEs with elliptic, hyperbolic and euclidean geometry.
we develop a generalization of VAEs to curved latent spaces that is both computationally efficient and easy to use.
we develop the mixed-curvature VAE which is a generalization of the Euclidean VEA to curved latent space, and recovers it as a special case.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mixed-curvature VAE can leverage the benefits of each curvature to learn better representations and achieve better performance on downstream tasks than any of its component curvature models.
the mixed-curvature VAE provides a unified framework for learning data representations in different curved latent spaces.
the mixed-curvature latent space is able to learn representations of data with different kinds of biases, which can then be exploited to solve tasks such as clustering and classification.
